chunks: we complain to You of the absence of our Prophet, the numerousness of our enemy and the diffusion of our passions.
ai.seo_question: What are the three main complaints made to God in the invocation when facing the enemy?
ai.summary: This supplication, often recited by Imam Ali (AS) before battle, reflects the spiritual and political struggles of the early Shia community, where 'absence' (ghaybah) can refer to both the Prophet's physical departure and the perceived distance of divine aid. It highlights the triad of challenges: external oppression (enemies), internal disunity (scattered desires), and the longing for prophetic guidance, serving as a model for communal resilience in times of trial.
